def count_bounded_run_arrangements(counts, m):
    """
    Count arrangements of a multiset of letters in which every maximal run
    of equal letters has length at most m.

    There are k = len(counts) distinct letter types; counts[i] >= 1 is the
    number of identical copies of letter type i.  An arrangement is a
    sequence using every copy exactly once; two arrangements are the same
    if their sequences of letter types are equal (copies of one type are
    indistinguishable).  A maximal run is a maximal contiguous block of
    equal letters.  Return the exact number of distinct arrangements whose
    maximal runs all have length <= m, as a Python int (0 if none exist).

    Input domain: counts is a non-empty list of ints with
    1 <= len(counts) <= 26, counts[i] >= 1, sum(counts) <= 150, and m is
    an int with 1 <= m <= sum(counts).  The answer is exact (arbitrary
    precision); no rounding, no modulus.

    Edge cases: with a single letter type the answer is 1 if
    counts[0] <= m, else 0.  If m >= sum(counts) the answer is the full
    multinomial coefficient.  Note m bounds the merged run, not the count
    per type: counts=[2], m=1 gives 0 because the two copies must touch.

    Naive enumeration is astronomically slow (the multinomial can exceed
    10^190), and a DP over remaining-count vectors is exponential in k.

    >>> count_bounded_run_arrangements([2, 1], 1)
    1
    >>> count_bounded_run_arrangements([3, 1], 2)
    2
    >>> count_bounded_run_arrangements([2, 2, 2], 1)
    30
    """
